scenarios.expected: Applying a group snapshots members into Approval requests; later group edits do not rewrite those requests. Non-Member+ selections and unauthorized configuration are refused; existing requests retain their recorded identities.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by an agent that did not write or source-review the guide; not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.
API sessions created prerequisites, played second actors' writes and read back saved state and refusals. Every guide step ran in the browser as the named role.

Other agents on this host create and remove lab networks. Chromium then aborted in-flight requests with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED and the app showed Something went wrong.; the scripts reload up to twice and log each retry under retries in the logs. 36 direct reloads of the affected Signatures pages afterwards showed no error page, so this is recorded as environment noise, not a product bug.

Run on the shared work lab (openlaw-docs-9d2b1705-work). Only DOC-032 contracts-2 groups, types, a fixture user and Contracts were created; the groups and types were archived after the run and the Approval permissions setting was put back.
Groups appear by name in the database collation, which ignores spaces and punctuation (DOC-032 contracts-2 ... sorts before DOC-032 contracts V-C16 ...). The walkthrough compares with the same rule.
One negative step ran as Nadia Haddad (Legal Team Member) to check that only an Administrator can open the page; the registry's role for V-C55 is Administrator.
